intro: Numbered practices, not dates. Rule 14.02 puts the first practice no earlier than July 15, and after that the calendar is yours — a rained-out session moves everything down one, it does not skip anything. Nothing here is installed before the thing it depends on, and the build refuses to publish a schedule that breaks that.

preseason.label: Before the first game
preseason.note: Thirteen plays and all four fronts. This is the whole package you can actually run in September — the Regular I both directions, a short-yardage answer, one play-action each way, and every defence the league lets us show. Do not add a formation until this is real.

season.label: Once the season starts
season.note: One new look at a time, and only when the last one has hurt somebody. Each of these exists because a defence has started cheating something — none of it is worth installing before that happens.

practices.focus: Stance, snap, and the first run
practices.emphasis: Alignment before anything. Count seven on the line every single snap, both sides of the ball, until it is boring.
The tailback reads the fullback's block. That is the skill this whole formation exists to teach — give it the time.
Down block and kick out. Say out loud that these are the same rules as Iso, one gap wider.
The carrier does not turn up until he is outside our end. Drill nothing else this session.
Counter is worthless until Toss has gone for real yards. If it has not yet, run Toss again and come back to this.
Fourth and inches, both sides of it. Install the goal-line front the same day so they see what a six-man line feels like.
No new offence. Spend it on the fourth linebacker and on reviewing everything from practices 1 to 6 against a front they have not seen.
Run first, throw second. No blitzing is allowed at this age, so the quarterback has time — teach him to be patient and look up.

practices.focus: The same throw the other way
practices.emphasis: Boot and Waggle are a matched pair. Call whichever one goes away from where their outside linebacker has started cheating.

practices.focus: The rules that are not optional
practices.emphasis: The 18-point rule is mandatory, not a coaching choice. Prevent, and the whole starting backfield coming out on offence, both have to be automatic before the first game — an official will not wait while you work it out.
Same eleven kids, same spots, flanker tightened to a wing. No line rule changes at all — say that first and they will believe it.
Two yards is a good wedge. Do not call it needing four. Re-check with the league that wedge blocking is still permitted this season.
Only one man may be moving at the snap and he cannot be moving toward the line. Teach the wing to run flat across, never forward.
The motion is only a lie if it has been the truth. Jet has to have hurt them before this is worth a down.

practices.focus: The wing hides in the backfield
practices.emphasis: Same play, same hole, same three jobs. At the wing he is a tell; in the backfield he is not, and the trade is a worse angle so he leaves on the snap.
Both of these are lies about Offset Power. Neither is worth a down until Offset Power has been run for real yards.
Three threats every snap. The fullback is the hammer — if they stop respecting him up the middle, nothing else in this formation works.
Symmetric formation, symmetric rules. They learn one play and get two — make that the whole pitch.
Four plays in one session only works because the rules are identical to Power. If they are not solid on Power, split this over two.
One pass in this formation is the right number. It exists so nobody can put nine in the box and forget the edge.
Same back numbers as the Wishbone and the same three jobs — carry, kick out, lead. A team that knows Bone calls already knows House calls.
Sweep is the same first three steps as Power taken all the way outside, and Boot is the lie about both. Install them in that order inside the session.
